# Go

<!-- Generated by bazel run //tools/docs/languages:languages_bin -- --write from go/lang.json and go/defs.bzl. Do not edit. -->

## Install

Add `rules_dx` to `MODULE.bazel`:

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<version>")
```

Load the rules from `@rules_dx//go:defs.bzl`:

```python
load("@rules_dx//go:defs.bzl", "go_library", "go_binary", "go_test")
```

## Rules

### `go_library`

```python
go_library(name, srcs, importpath, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Minimal wrapper over go_library.

### `go_binary`

```python
go_binary(name, *, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Minimal wrapper over go_binary. cgo is off unless set.

### `go_test`

```python
go_test(name, *, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Minimal wrapper over go_test. cgo is off unless set.

### `go_fuzz_test`

```python
go_fuzz_test(name, *, srcs = None, target, visibility = None, tags = None, **kwargs)
```

A go_test plus a `<name>_run` runner that fuzzes the function `target` for `dx fuzz`.

### `go_bench`

```python
go_bench(name, *, srcs = None, visibility = None, tags = None, **kwargs)
```

A go_test of the Benchmark functions plus a `<name>` runner that writes dx-bench.json for `dx bench`.

## API docs

Tool: `go doc`.

```python
load("@rules_dx//tools/docs/go:defs.bzl", "go_doc_shard")
```

### `go_doc_shard`

```python
go_doc_shard(name, library, package = "", goos = "linux", goarch = "amd64", build_tags = [], **kwargs)
```

Declares the DocIr shard of one Go library.

Build the docs with `tools/dx docs`; see [docs](../cli/commands/docs.md).

## Dependencies

Add the module to `go.mod` and wire it in `MODULE.bazel`:

```starlark
go = use_extension("@rules_dx//go:extensions.bzl", "go")
go.from_file(go_mod = "//:go.mod")
```

Then run `dx generate --apply`. An import under a module that `go.mod`
requires directly resolves to `@<repo>//<package>`. A module required only as
`// indirect` fails with a hint to require it directly.

## Toolchain

### cgo

Ordinary cgo, meaning C sources and C++ through `cdeps` over a C ABI, runs with
LLVM (the default) and with GCC on Linux x86_64 and arm64. Under GCC, libstdc++
links statically. Race mode has its own test target (`gcc_cgo_race_test`) so a
race failure never hides ordinary cgo. Windows and MSVC are not supported yet.

cgo needs a GNU-style C++ driver and ABI. With `cgo = True`, an MSVC or clang-cl
toolchain fails at analysis, because rules_go would otherwise build the package
without cgo.
